title: Signature Template matching — Optical Character Recognition Engine
description: Signature original — Template matching slides character prototypes over the image, scoring pixel agreement. It works on clean, fixed fonts with known layouts. Templates are the simplest real OCR. This record documents a Signature-authored original method of the JAH archive toolkit, clearly labeled as Signature work rather than a public record.
demo:
# OCR by template matching: 3x5 pixel digit templates matched against an input row.
templates = {'1': ['..#..', '..#..', '..#..', '..#..', '..#..'], '2': ['.###.', '....#', '.###.', '#....', '.###.']}
def render(line):
    # line: string of chars present in templates -> pixel rows
    rows = [""] * 5
    for ch in line:
        t = templates[ch]
        for i in range(5): rows[i] += t[i] + " "
    return rows
def recognize(rows):
    out = ""
    nchars = len(rows[0]) // 6
    for c in range(nchars):
        block = [r[c*6:c*6+5] for r in rows]
        best, bs = "?", -1
        for ch, t in templates.items():
            score = sum(a == b for ra, rb in zip(block, t) for a, b in zip(ra, rb))
            if score > bs: best, bs = ch, score
        out += best
    return out
rows = render("12")
print("\n".join(rows))
print("recognized:", recognize(rows))
provenance: Signature-authored original method created for the JAH archive toolkit; clearly labeled Signature, not a public record.
